strings.finding.recovery.environment-off.title: This PC has no working recovery environment
strings.finding.recovery.environment-off.benefit: The recovery environment is what runs Startup Repair, System Restore and Reset when Windows will not start. Without it, a PC that fails to boot needs a USB recovery drive made on another computer.
strings.finding.recovery.environment-off.safety: Nothing is changed by this check. Turning the recovery environment back on is a repair worth doing while the PC still starts normally — this version does not do it for you.
strings.finding.recovery.environment-staged.titl: A recovery environment update was left half-applied
strings.finding.recovery.environment-staged.bene: The recovery environment is registered but marked as mid-update, so it will not start when you need it. Finishing or undoing that update restores the rescue path.
strings.finding.recovery.environment-staged.safe: Nothing is changed by this check. This state usually comes from an interrupted Windows update and is worth resolving before the next restart.
strings.finding.recovery.restore-point-stale.tit: The newest restore point is {days} days old
strings.finding.recovery.restore-point-stale.ben: System Restore is on, but the last point it kept is from {days} days ago. Restoring that far back undoes months of updates, so in practice this is protection you would not use.
strings.finding.recovery.restore-point-stale.saf: Nothing is changed by this check. Anything newer than about {threshold} days is a restore you would actually be willing to run; older than that usually means the disk space allowed for restore points is too small.
strings.finding.workload.windows11-not-ready.tit: This PC does not meet {count, plural, one {# Windows 11 requirement} other {# Windows 11 requirements}} yet
strings.finding.workload.windows11-not-ready.ben: Windows 11 needs UEFI boot, Secure Boot and a TPM 2.0 security chip.
What is missing is switched off in firmware rather than absent from this machine. That is a setting you change once, in the setup screen, in a few minutes — not a reason to replace the PC.
What is missing is not something a setting can turn on for this machine, so no plan here will make it eligible. Knowing that now is worth more than trying things that cannot work.
strings.finding.workload.windows11-not-ready.saf: Nothing is changed by this check. Anything listed as unreadable was not counted against this PC — it was simply not visible to the scan.

strings.finding.firmware.bios-old.title: The BIOS on this PC is about {years} years old
strings.finding.firmware.bios-old.benefit.window: This machine can receive firmware through Windows Update, so a newer BIOS may already be waiting there. Firmware updates carry security fixes that Windows updates cannot.
strings.finding.firmware.bios-old.benefit.vendor: This machine does not publish the table Windows Update needs to deliver firmware, so a newer BIOS will never arrive on its own — it only comes from the manufacturers own page for {model}.
strings.finding.firmware.bios-old.safety: An old BIOS is not a fault, and this app will not change it. Firmware is the one thing here where a mistake means a PC that does not turn on, so flashing it stays your decision, made with the manufacturers own tool.

strings.cli.checkup.ok.body: Nothing needs attention. We checked virtualization, memory speed, refresh rate, System Restore, restore point freshness, the recovery environment, Windows 11 requirements, firmware age, privacy settings, feature dependencies and drive encryption.
strings.app.protection.title: What is defending this PC
strings.app.protection.tamperOn: Windows is guarding these settings, so nothing outside Windows Security can change them — including this app.
strings.app.protection.tamperOff: Tamper Protection is off, so these settings can be changed from outside Windows Security.
strings.app.protection.weakenRefused: This app will not switch your protection off. If you have decided to, Windows Security is where it is done — and it will still be your decision there, not a side effect of a cleanup.
strings.finding.security.smartscreen-off.title: SmartScreen is switched off
strings.finding.security.smartscreen-off.benefit: SmartScreen is what warns you before a downloaded program that nobody else has run yet. With it off, that warning does not appear.
strings.finding.security.smartscreen-off.safety: Turning it back on changes nothing about programs you already trust — it only adds the warning for ones Windows has not seen before.
strings.finding.security.realtime-off.title: Defender real-time protection is off
strings.finding.security.realtime-off.benefit: Nothing is scanning files as they are opened. If another antivirus is installed this is normal and expected; if not, this machine is unprotected right now.
strings.finding.security.realtime-off.safety: This app does not change it either way. Windows Security is where it is turned back on.

strings.cli.clean.regenerable: rebuilt on demand — freed at once
strings.cli.clean.reportOnly: shown only — this app will not remove it
strings.cli.clean.confirm: Reclaim {mb} MB? Caches that rebuild themselves are deleted and the space comes back now; everything else moves to quarantine and can be restored for 30 days. Cookies, history and saved passwords are never touched. Type y to continue.
strings.cli.restore.purged: Emptied the quarantine and released {mb} MB. Nothing in it can be restored now.
strings.cli.restore.how: Put one back with: pco restore <id>. Free the space now with: pco restore purge
strings.app.section.apps.sub: Install software, set up Office, and change Windows itself
strings.app.apps.title: Software this app installs
strings.app.apps.hint: Everything here comes from Microsoft’s own package repository, which checks what it downloads against a published hash. This is the whole list: this app cannot install anything that is not on it.
strings.app.apps.unavailable: winget is not on this machine, so nothing here can be installed. It comes with App Installer from the Microsoft Store.
strings.app.apps.unreadable: Could not ask which of these are already installed, so every row shows Install. Installing something that is already there is harmless — winget will say so.
strings.app.apps.done: {name} is installed, and the machine agrees it is there.
strings.app.apps.removedDone: {name} is gone, and the machine agrees.
strings.app.apps.unverified: The command finished, but asking the machine again does not show {name} the way we expected. Nothing has been claimed that was not checked.
strings.app.apps.confirmInstall:
Install {name} from {publisher}?

This downloads and runs the publisher’s own installer through Microsoft’s package repository.
strings.app.apps.confirmRemove:
Remove {name}?

Anything it saved on this PC may go with it. This app cannot put that back.
strings.app.office.stateNote: Read from the machine, not from a licence file.
strings.app.office.planHint: This uses Microsoft’s own Office Deployment Tool and downloads from Microsoft’s servers. It ships no product key and works around no licensing: after it installs, sign in with the account the licence belongs to.
strings.app.office.confirm:
Install {product}?

This downloads several gigabytes from Microsoft and can take a while. You will need to sign in afterwards with the account the licence belongs to — this app supplies no key.
strings.app.office.completed: Office finished installing. Sign in to activate it.
strings.app.licence.title: Windows activation
strings.app.licence.note: Read from Windows’ own licensing service. This app never supplies, generates or bypasses a product key.
strings.app.licence.warnBeforeChange: Activate Windows before changing the edition. Changing it while it is unactivated tends to leave a machine that is both.
strings.app.edition.title: Windows edition
strings.app.edition.hint: Windows can move up an edition in place, without reinstalling and without touching your files. It cannot move down.
strings.app.edition.none: Windows offers no edition to change to on this PC.
strings.app.edition.unreadable: Could not ask Windows which editions it offers: {problem}
strings.app.edition.keyNote: Changing edition needs a product key for the edition you are moving to. This app does not have one and will not make one up — buy it from Microsoft, then enter it in Settings › System › Activation.
strings.app.reinstall.title: Reinstall Windows from a disc image
strings.app.reinstall.hint: Repairs Windows in place from an ISO you already have, keeping your files and — if you choose — your apps. No USB stick is needed. Download the ISO from Microsoft.
strings.app.reinstall.notWindows: That file does not look like Windows installation media.
strings.app.reinstall.scope.everything: Keep my files and my apps
strings.app.reinstall.scope.filesOnly: Keep my files, reinstall my apps myself
strings.app.reinstall.launched: Windows Setup has started. Follow its own prompts from here.
strings.app.reinstall.ready: Nothing is standing in the way. Windows Setup will take it from here.
strings.app.office.stage.tool: Fetching Microsoft’s deployment tool, then downloading and installing Office. This runs as one long step and can take half an hour or more — you can leave this page open.
